title: Career Roadmap: Junior Machine Learning Engineer
summary: A Junior Machine Learning Engineer develops, tests, and deploys machine learning models that learn patterns from data and help solve real-world problems. The role combines programming, mathematics, data processing, model evaluation, and software engineering.

blocks.text: For students pursuing a B.Sc. in Artificial Intelligence or Machine Learning, the main objective is to build strong Python and mathematics fundamentals, complete practical ML projects, and demonstrate the ability to turn a model into a usable application.

blocks.text: A crucial skill is understanding why a model works and when it fails—not simply knowing how to call a library. The official scikit-learn guide covers model fitting, preprocessing, pipelines, cross-validation, and parameter search.
scikit-learn 1.9.1 documentation
Python and Jupyter Notebook
Use Python as the primary language and notebooks for experimentation. Learn to move reusable code into proper Python modules.
scikit-learn
Start with classical ML, preprocessing, pipelines, metrics, and model selection. Official getting-started guide
TensorFlow or PyTorch
Learn one framework for neural networks after mastering classical ML.

GitHub

Aim for three or four polished projects rather than many copied notebooks.
Project 1 — Predictive analytics
Build a house-price, customer-churn, or demand-prediction model.

blocks.label: Demonstrates
blocks.text: data cleaning, feature engineering, regression or classification, metrics, and error analysis.
Project 2 — Computer vision
Create an image classifier or object-detection prototype using a suitable public dataset.

blocks.label: Demonstrates
blocks.text: dataset preparation, image preprocessing, model evaluation, and error inspection.
Project 3 — Natural language processing
Build a sentiment classifier or document categorisation system.

blocks.label: Demonstrates
blocks.text: text preprocessing, feature extraction or embeddings, evaluation, and prediction.
Project 4 — End-to-end ML application
Train a model, expose it through a FastAPI endpoint, add input validation and tests, and deploy it.

blocks.label: Demonstrates
blocks.text: model serialization, API integration, software engineering, and deployment.

For each project, document the problem, dataset source, baseline, evaluation metric, limitations, and instructions to reproduce the result. Never report training accuracy as proof that a model generalises well.

Prepare for interview rounds covering Python, SQL, data structures and algorithms, statistics, ML fundamentals, project discussions, and basic deployment. A B.Sc. candidate should also be ready to explain how their academic background meets the role's requirements.

Compensation varies by location, company, degree requirements, interview performance, and whether the job is genuinely ML engineering or a broader data/AI role. Entry-level offers can vary widely, so validate estimates against current vacancies and actual job offers.
Compare roles by responsibilities, learning opportunities, mentorship, and fixed pay rather than relying on the job title alone.

blocks.label: Final recommendation
blocks.text: Start with Python, statistics, SQL, and classical ML. Then build a complete model-to-API project and use it to demonstrate both machine-learning knowledge and software-engineering ability. For a B.Sc. graduate, a credible project portfolio and strong fundamentals can help distinguish you in junior-level applications, although individual employers may have additional degree requirements.
